new_entities.name: High serum PFAS burden
aliases: elevated serum per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances
new_entities.description: Above-background serum concentrations of per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances measured in human biospecimens.

new_entities.name: LDL elevation
new_entities.description: An upward shift in low-density lipoprotein cholesterol concentration associated with exposure or intervention.

edges.effect_quant: A 2023 adult meta-analysis found that each interquartile-range increase in PFOA was associated with a 1.4 mg/dL rise in LDL-C (95% CI 0.6 to 2.2), while PFOS was associated with a 1.9 mg/dL rise (95% CI 0.9 to 3.0). Longitudinal follow-up in a highly exposed Italian population also showed that declines in PFAS were accompanied by decreases in LDL-C, supporting a reversible association.
edges.population: general adult populations with serum PFAS measurements from NHANES, exposed regional cohorts, or pooled epidemiologic studies
edges.mechanism: PFAS appear to interact with lipid metabolism, bile-acid handling, and hepatic transport pathways in ways that can shift LDL concentrations upward. The effect size is usually modest, but the consistency across population studies makes the lipid signal one of the more reproducible human PFAS findings.
edges.summary: High serum PFAS burden is consistently associated with modest LDL elevation in adults. The average shift is not large enough to explain dyslipidemia on its own, but it is reproducible enough that PFAS exposure looks more like a real lipid risk modifier than a statistical curiosity.
edges.caveats: Most studies are observational and compound-specific, with stronger signals for PFOA and PFOS than for every PFAS class. This edge supports PFAS as a modest dyslipidemia contributor, not as a dominant cause of high LDL in the absence of other risk factors.
